title: Simulation-Based Super-Resolution Kikuchi Pattern Analysis
content: This work presents a method for analyzing Kikuchi patterns measured in electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) by combining high-resolution Kikuchi pattern simulations with a simulation-based supersampling strategy to determine orientations and relative deformation gradient tensors from experimentally acquired low-resolution images [1]. The approach is motivated by the challenge of extracting quantitative strain and orientation information from EBSD data acquired with lower bit depth and fewer pixels, while maintaining a high level of precision. In the proposed method, a high-fidelity simulation of the Kikuchi diffraction pattern is used as a reference that is continuously rotated and deformed according to a model based on projective geometry and finite strain theory. The deformation gradient tensor is expressed via its polar decomposition into a rotational part and an isochoric (volume-preserving) stretch, which in turn allows one to derive a Biot strain tensor that approximates the infinitesimal strain in the small deformation regime.
